question: Which check or mutation tools should .config/dotnet-tools.json bind?

census.method: Every markdown, workflow, python file and project file was searched for 'dotnet tool', dotnet-ef, dotnet-format, dotnet-coverage, reportgenerator and stryker. Nothing matched outside historical evidence. The API surface tools shell out to git and to 'dotnet run' on a project in this repository; no external tool is invoked anywhere.
census.designTimeEfUsage: none. The migration hosted services under src and benchmarks are runtime code; there is no design time migration that would need dotnet-ef.

consequence: There is no tool the repository uses today, so a manifest can only be empty - which the directive forbids - or it introduces a tool that is not used today, which is a new entry in the frozen dependency contract. Section 7 says that choice is a question before the edit, so no manifest was written.

options.title: Bind Stryker.NET as the mutation tool and use it for the product assemblies
options.pro: Mutation testing is currently done by hand - a byte snapshot, an edit, a run, a restore - which is honest but not repeatable by anybody else and covers only the mutation somebody thought of. A tool makes the survivor set a measurement.
options.contra: A substantial new dependency, and a full mutation run over this product is expensive in wall clock. It would also need its own place in the verification model.

options.title: No manifest, and say why in docs/build.md
options.pro: Nothing is bound that nothing uses. The repository stays exactly as reproducible as it is now.
options.contra: The directive asks for a manifest, and a later contributor may install a tool globally and use it without anything noticing.

options.title: No manifest, plus a policy rule that refuses any documented or scripted use of a tool that is not bound
options.pro: Answers the risk the directive names - an unbound globally installed tool - without inventing a dependency. The first genuine need then arrives as a rule failure rather than as a habit.
options.contra: Still no manifest file, so the letter of the directive is unmet until a tool is genuinely needed.

recommendation: OPT-GUARD-ONLY, with OPT-STRYKER as a separate decision once the mutation practice is meant to become a gate rather than a discipline.
